title: Cross-Functional Rollout Taproot: KPI Cadence & Readiness Tracker
body:
Summary:
This sheet introduces a Taproot method for launch readiness: pick a single primary outcome metric (the taproot) and maintain a lightweight lattice of supporting signals (roots) across teams so we can rapidly triage causal drift. The tracker is built to be both a weekly cadence log and an on-call lightweight playbook for T-7 to T+14 around launches.

Objective:
- Reduce ambiguity in go/no-go decisions by surfacing a single prioritized metric per rollout plus 6–10 supporting signals spanning latency, cost, error rate, user adoption, and qualitative quality checks.
- Create a reproducible cadence (daily -> weekly) for signal review and decision handoffs.

How to use this file:
1) Set the Taproot metric at the top of the sheet (one metric only). 2) Fill supporting signals (team owner + measurement window). 3) Use color-coded cells (green/amber/red) to record signal health at each cadence tick. 4) Add short notes only for anomalies — keep long investigations in linked artifacts.

Taproot choice rationale (example):
- Taproot = 95th percentile host latency for generation requests under 1k tokens (because product SLAs and direct cost/throughput coupling).
- Supporting signals: Dedicated queue utilization, average token cost, model fallback rate, prefix-cache hit rate, error-rate by region, customer-reported quality regressions.

KPI Tracker (columns explained then sample rows):
Columns: Week | Taproot (value) | Taproot trend (▲/▼/—) | Owner | Top 3 roots summary | Root health snapshot | Risk escalation (Y/N) | Action items (owner, ETA) | Notes / investigation links
Sample rows (format: CSV style):
2024-11-11, 430ms (95p), ▲, Eng - Serving Runtime (Marcus), queue util 78% / fallback 3% / cost $0.003/token, amber / green / green, Y, "Temp scale up pool (Devon) by 2024-11-13", "confluence://incident/latency-spike-1111"
2024-11-18, 410ms (95p), ▼, Eng - Serving Runtime (Marcus), queue util 72% / fallback 2% / cost $0.0028/token, green / green / green, N, "monitor only", ""

Acceptance criteria per signal (short checklist):
- Latency: 95p < 500ms for hosted tier; if amber > 2 consecutive ticks, trigger capacity runbook.
- Cost: unit token cost within -10%/+15% of target; if > +15% sustained across tick, pause noncritical heavy prompts.
- Fallback rate: < 5% sustained; if > 5% alert product and SRE.
- Cache hit rate: > 35% for common prefixes; failures reduce cost savings estimate.

Launch readiness quick checklist (T-7 to T+0):
- T-7: Finalize taproot and owners. Confirm dedicated capacity staging and run basic smoke (50 QPS) — owner: DevOps (Devon).
- T-5: Confirm monitoring dashboards live for all roots (Latency, Cost, Errors, Fallbacks, Quality flags) — owner: Observability (Sofia).
- T-3: Run canary traffic (1% production) for 24h with automated rollback watch — owner: Product (Aisha).
- T-1: Stakeholder sync and go/no-go poll using Taproot value + top 2 roots. Must have explicit mitigation plans for amber taps.
- T0: Go or hold recorded in this tracker with timestamp and approvers. Toggle traffic plan executed by Release Engineering.

Post-launch (T+1 to T+14) stabilization cadence:
- Daily (T+1 to T+3): EOD taproot snapshot + incident triage if any amber/red signal. Rapid rollback allowed if taproot degrades > 25% vs baseline and no clear mitigation.
- Bi-daily (T+4 to T+14): Morning check-in if any ongoing escalations; otherwise weekly sync on day 7 for adoption/quality review.

Rapid triage playbook (short):
1) Identify whether taproot or a root is failing. 2) If a root: apply targeted containment (scale, q-limit, route to fallback) and note in action items. 3) If taproot: immediate escalations to SRE + Product; consider canary rollback if impacts user-facing quality.

Risk triggers and mitigation matrix (examples):
- Sudden jump in 95p latency + queue util > 85% -> mitigation: scale dedicated pool + enable short-term traffic shaping for heavy prompts.
- Token cost spike when cache hit rate drops -> mitigation: disable expensive feature flags and roll forward QC of quantization profile.
- Increase in model fallback rate -> mitigation: route to smaller model variant and open model-oncall review.

Ownership & decision authority (table in-brief):
- Product (Aisha) = final go/no-go authority for feature visible to users.
- Eng - Serving Runtime (Marcus) = technical health signoff (latency/capacity).
- Observability (Sofia) = signal integrity & dashboard accuracy.
- Release Eng (Devon) = traffic execution and rollback.

Next steps / proposed cadence for product-ops team:
- Adopt this sheet as canonical short-lived cadence for each launch. Keep long investigations in separate Confluence pages and link.
- Run dry-run with upcoming small feature (internal beta) before using for major launches.

Notes & references:
- Lightweight: keep note fields under 120 chars; link to Confluence/Jira for deep investigations.
- Example linked artifacts: confluence://prodops/taproot-postmortem-2024-09, JIRA-POPS-1023 (canary-rollout-test).

Change log:
- 2024-11-12 created by Aisha Patel (initial template and taproot rationale)
- 2024-11-18 sample data added and owners updated (Marcus, Sofia, Devon)
- 2024-12-03 minor wording edits and acceptance thresholds revised

End of document.
